# Thermalyn Pro launch creative

## 1. Copy

### Landing-page hero

| Element | Copy | Count |
|---|---|---|
| H1 | Less HVAC energy.¹ No more thermostat fights. | 7 words |
| Subhead | Thermalyn Pro learns your opening hours, limits staff changes to ±2°F, and alerts you when a door's open with the HVAC running. | 22 words |
| CTA button | Order Thermalyn Pro | 3 words / 19 chars |
| Price line (beside CTA) | $149 launch price (list $179) + $8/month per location for Corbel Cloud. Launch price ends Jan 31, 2026. | 18 words |
| Proof line | Pilot sites cut HVAC energy use by a median 18%.¹ 44 of 48 found it easier than their old thermostat. | 20 words |
| Footnote | ¹ Based on a 2025 pilot of 48 small-business sites. Results vary. | 12 words |

**Below-the-fold quote (optional, pending confirmation; see note):**
*"Our summer bill dropped by about $210 a month, and nobody fights over the thermostat anymore."*¹ Jane Doe, owner, Doe & Daughters Bakery. This is a total-bill claim, so it carries the same footnote.

### Meta feed ad (1080×1080)

| Element | Copy | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Headline | Your thermostat, off your to-do list | 36 chars |
| Primary text | Learns your hours, caps staff changes at ±2°F, flags open doors. Until Jan 31: $149 + $8/mo per location for Corbel Cloud. | 122 chars |
| On-image text | Staff get ±2°F. That's it. | 5 words |

The ad makes no savings claim. The required footnote alone is 65 characters, which leaves too little room in the 125-character primary text. It also exceeds the 6-word image limit. Savings are covered on the landing page, where the footnote fits.

### Google responsive search ad

| Element | Copy | Count |
|---|---|---|
| Headline 1 | Small business thermostat | 25 chars |
| Headline 2 | Learns your opening hours | 25 chars |
| Headline 3 | $149 + $8/mo per location | 25 chars |
| Description 1 | Caps staff changes at ±2°F and alerts you when a door's open with the HVAC running. | 83 chars |
| Description 2 | Launch price $149 (list $179) until Jan 31, 2026. Corbel Cloud $8/mo per location. | 82 chars |

Every price element states the subscription on its own line. This matters because Google mixes headlines and descriptions at random, so no combination can show $149 without the $8/month. There are no savings claims, for the same footnote reason as the Meta ad.

---

## 2. Layout and visual direction

### Landing-page hero (1200×630)

**Hierarchy, top to bottom, left column (about 65% width):**
1. **Eyebrow:** "For cafés, salons and shops", 14px Inter Semibold, Deep Spruce, with a small Signal Amber dot.
2. **H1:** 44–48px Inter Bold, Deep Spruce, two lines. The line break sits after "energy." so each half reads as its own point.
3. **Subhead:** 20px Inter Regular, Deep Spruce at about 85% opacity, three lines maximum.
4. **CTA row:**
   - The button is Signal Amber with Deep Spruce text. Do not use white on amber, because it fails contrast.
   - The price line sits immediately to the right in 14px, so the price and subscription are always read together.
5. **Proof line:** 16px, sits below a thin Deep Spruce hairline divider.
6. **Footnote:** 12px, Deep Spruce at 70% opacity. It sits directly under the proof line, inside the hero and above the fold. Never move it to the page footer.

**Right panel (about 35% width):**
- Use a solid Deep Spruce block.
- Show the device on the wall, photographed straight-on in natural daylight. Use a real café or salon wall (tile, plaster, a menu board edge) rather than a white void.
- Overlay one Signal Amber alert chip ("Back door open, HVAC on") to show the open-door feature without explaining it.

**Colour use:**
- Paper is the field.
- Deep Spruce carries all text and the image panel.
- Signal Amber is limited to accents: the CTA, the alert chip, the device ring and the eyebrow dot. Keep amber under about 10% of the frame.

**Imagery tone:**
- Show the owner's world: early morning, chairs still up, someone flipping the sign.
- Avoid people pointing at thermostats, and avoid high-fives.

### Meta feed ad (1080×1080)

- **Image:** a tight crop of Thermalyn Pro on a salon or café wall. A staff member's hand reaches toward it, mid-adjustment. The screen shows only "71°" so it doesn't add to the on-image word count.
- **On-image text:**
  - "Staff get ±2°F. That's it." sits top-left on a Paper band of about 22% of the height.
  - Type is 72–80px Inter Bold in Deep Spruce, with "±2°F" in Signal Amber. Amber is acceptable here only because the type is large and bold.
- **Brand:** the Corbel wordmark sits bottom-right, small, in Paper on the photo.
- **Footnote:** none is needed, because there is no savings claim. If a savings variant is ever approved, the footnote must appear in full in the primary text, which means rewriting that text.
- **Safe zones:** keep text out of the bottom 15%, where Meta's UI overlays.

## 4. Note to product marketing

> Three changes.
>
> 1) **Headline:** "40%" isn't supported. It's HVAC's share of a typical bill. The median pilot site cut HVAC energy 18%, roughly 7% of the total bill, and only one site passed 40%. I've used the median, labelled as HVAC energy, with the required footnote.
>
> 2) **Price:** schedules and alerts need Corbel Cloud, so every $149 now appears with "+ $8/month per location" and the Jan 31 end date.
>
> 3) **Meta and Google:** they carry no savings claims, because the footnote won't fit their limits.
>
> Also: the Doe & Daughters quote is a total-bill claim, so it needs the footnote. "Jane Doe" also reads like a placeholder. Please confirm she's a real, consenting customer before it ships.

*(116 words)*
